answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token stake before it may submit work, then slash that stake when independently checked tasks reveal fraud. The stake is not proof that an agent is honest, but it makes a Sybil attack costly: splitting into many identities requires locking capital for each, and coordinating them does not avoid losing funds when false results are caught. A tundra, mesa, and zephyr task can share the same verification rule, so changing names or domains does not bypass the cost.
